sections.title: Issue #482: Date picker shows the wrong day

parts.heading: Issue description
parts.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Issue #482, opened by user maria-dev. Title: Date picker shows the wrong day in some time zones. Labels: bug, needs-reproduction. When I select the first of the month, the form saves the last day of the previous month. This happens only on my staging site. On my laptop everything works. I use version 3.4.0 of the library and I expected that the date I click is the date that is saved. This is a problem for our billing page because invoices get the wrong date. Thanks for the great library!

parts.heading: Steps to reproduce
parts.content: Steps to reproduce, added by maria-dev after a request: 1. Set the computer time zone to Pacific Time (UTC minus 8). 2. Open the example page of the date picker. 3. Click the first day of any month. 4. Press Save and read the saved value. Expected: the first day of the month. Actual: the last day of the previous month. Environment: Chrome 124 and Firefox 125, macOS 14, library version 3.4.0, Node 20. The bug does not appear when the time zone is UTC or a time zone east of UTC.

parts.heading: Maintainer comment
parts.content: Comment by maintainer ken-lib. Thanks for the clear steps, Maria. I can reproduce this. The cause is that the picker creates the date at midnight in UTC and then formats it in the local time zone. In time zones west of UTC, midnight in UTC is still the previous evening, so the day moves back. This is a real bug and it affects every date picked in those time zones. I have added the label confirmed and removed needs-reproduction. As a workaround, you can pass the option useLocalTime set to true, which creates dates at local midnight.

parts.heading: Community comments
parts.content: Comment by dev-tom: The workaround works for me. I added useLocalTime and my tests pass. Comment by sara-codes: Please note that useLocalTime changes the value that the library gives to your onChange handler, so you may need to update tests that compare exact timestamps. Comment by maria-dev: Confirmed on my staging site, invoices have the correct date now. I will keep the option until the fix is released. Is there a date for the release?

parts.heading: Fix and status
parts.content: Comment by ken-lib: A fix is ready in pull request #490. It changes the default so that dates are created in local time, and it adds tests for time zones from UTC minus 12 to UTC plus 14. The fix will be released in version 3.4.1 next Tuesday. Because it changes how values are created, the release notes will mention it, and the useLocalTime option will be deprecated. Status: closed as completed when 3.4.1 is published. Thanks to everyone who helped with reproduction.

performanceTask.title: Write a helpful reply on an issue
performanceTask.scenario: Bạn đọc một issue và viết một câu trả lời giúp người báo lỗi và người duy trì thư viện.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Đọc đoạn issue ngắn rồi viết một câu trả lời bằng tiếng Anh (60 đến 110 từ): xác nhận bạn tái hiện được, nêu môi trường và gợi ý cách tạm. Chưa xem bài mẫu.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Write a helpful reply on the issue in English, 60 to 110 words: say whether you can reproduce it, give your environment and suggest a workaround or next step.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Thanks for the clear steps, Maria. I can reproduce this on Chrome 124 with the time zone set to Pacific Time and library version 3.4.0. Expected: the first day of the month. Actual: the last day of the previous month. It does not happen in UTC. As a workaround, you can set useLocalTime to true, but please check tests that compare exact timestamps. Pull request #490 should fix the root cause and is planned for 3.4.1 next Tuesday. I can test the fix on our staging site and report the result here.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Write the reply again in English. Keep it friendly and make the workaround clearer.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: Write a reply for a different issue, using reproduction, environment and a workaround.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Write a reply for another issue without looking at old notes.
